title: Archaeal Type II tRNA V Arms and the Pre-Coding to Coding Transition
content: Background/Objectives: A fundamental question is how the first genetic code arose. Type II tRNAs are an essential part of this history. In Archaea, tRNALeu (5 tRNALeu) and tRNASer (4 tRNASer) are type II tRNAs. Methods: To analyze type II tRNA V arms, bioinformatics and network analyses were applied to a large archaeal tRNA database. Available structures were considered to support the analyses. Conclusions: Type II V arms for archaeal tRNALeu and tRNASer diverged early, in pre-life. Candidates for the earliest archaeal tRNALeu and tRNASer sequences have been identified by network analysis and proximity to type II tRNAPri (Pri for primordial). Almost all tRNALeu V arms appear to have radiated from the ancient sequence V1-UGGCGAAGGCCUGC-V14. The 5’-V2-GGC-V4 tRNALeu V arm stem motif is conserved in many tRNASer V arms. In tRNALeu, V6-AAG-V8 binds LeuRS-IA. The LeuRS-IA V arm end loop binding site is abolished in tRNASer V arms. The number of unpaired bases (2 if by Leu and one if by Ser) separating the 3’-V arm stem and the Levitt base Vn (V arm of length n nucleotides) gives the trajectory of the arm. For both tRNALeu and tRNASer V arms, V1U interacts with tRNA-G26, and VnC interacts with tRNA-G15 (the Levitt base pair). That a primitive tRNASer was derived from a primitive tRNALeu by remodeling the V arm is proposed.
